name: Prasugrel
route_note: oral tablet once daily after a loading dose
originator: Daiichi Sankyo and Ube Industries; co-developed with Eli Lilly

discovery.note: Third-generation thienopyridine designed for more efficient activation than clopidogrel.

tagline: Third-generation thienopyridine with faster, stronger platelet inhibition
summary: Prasugrel is a thienopyridine prodrug that irreversibly blocks the P2Y12 ADP receptor on platelets. It is used with aspirin in acute coronary syndrome patients undergoing coronary intervention, giving more potent inhibition than clopidogrel but more bleeding.
mechanism: Prasugrel is rapidly hydrolysed by intestinal esterases to a thiolactone, which a single cytochrome P450-dependent step (CYP3A4 and CYP2B6) converts to the active metabolite.

The active metabolite covalently binds P2Y12 and blocks ADP-induced platelet activation for the platelet's life span. Its more efficient activation makes it less dependent on CYP2C19 genotype than clopidogrel.
uses: Acute coronary syndrome managed with percutaneous coronary intervention (with aspirin)

history.title: TRITON-TIMI 38
history.detail: Prasugrel reduces ischaemic events versus clopidogrel in ACS with PCI, but increases major bleeding.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Approved in the EU as Efient (February).

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US as Effient with a boxed bleeding warning (July).

history.title: TRILOGY ACS
history.detail: No benefit over clopidogrel in medically managed ACS without revascularisation.

history.title: ISAR-REACT 5
history.detail: A prasugrel-based strategy outperforms ticagrelor in ACS patients planned for invasive management.

pk.metabolism: Esterase hydrolysis then CYP3A4/2B6 to active metabolite

safety.boxed_warning: Significant, sometimes fatal bleeding; contraindicated after prior TIA or stroke; generally not recommended at age ≥75; lower dose for weight <60 kg; avoid starting in patients likely to undergo CABG.

facts: Patients with prior stroke or TIA had net harm in TRITON-TIMI 38, leading to a contraindication.

references.title: Wiviott SD et al. Prasugrel versus clopidogrel in patients with acute coronary syndromes (TRITON-TIMI 38). N Engl J Med 2007
